code:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import (
    CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer)
docs = ["battery lasts all day",
        "battery died after one day",
        "screen is bright and sharp",
        "screen cracked after one day"]
cv = CountVectorizer()
X = cv.fit_transform(docs)
X.shape   # (4, 13)
caption: Illustrative reviews. 4 documents, 13 distinct words.

code:
df = pd.DataFrame(X.toarray(),
    columns=cv.get_feature_names_out())
df[["battery","day","died","screen"]]

   battery  day  died  screen
0        1    1     0       0
1        1    1     1       0
2        0    0     0       1
3        0    1     0       1
caption: X itself is sparse: 63% of its cells are zero.

code:
tf = TfidfVectorizer()
T = tf.fit_transform(docs)

# learned IDF (scikit-learn's smoothed)
# day      1.22   in 3 of 4 docs
# battery  1.51   in 2 of 4 docs
# died     1.92   in 1 of 4 docs
caption: Rarer word, higher weight. Rows are scaled to length 1.

code:
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import (
    cosine_similarity)

q = tf.transform(["the battery died"])
cosine_similarity(q, T).round(2)
# [[0.28 0.7  0.   0.  ]]
caption: Nearest: review 1. Words unseen in fitting ('the') are ignored.
